say: Got bumped from my hour again. Some of us plan our whole week around this.
Ice was chewed. Pucks were hopping. Not a good session.
@how_are_things

options.text: I'm sorry. What would make it better?
It's an old building. Bear with us.
Rinks are hard. Take it or leave it.

say: Bucket of pucks, empty net. I'll talk, but I'm still shooting.
{event}. Five people out here. It's paradise.
Working on the backhand. It's a long project. Years.

options.text: What are you working on?
I'll leave you to it.

say: Early hour, best hour. Nobody here but me and the echo.
Morning. Ice is fresh. Don't talk too loud, you'll wake it.

options.text: Good to see you anyway.

say: {owner}. Grab a stick. I'll feed you a few.
Hey. Thanks for keeping the hour. Means a lot. That's all I'll say.

options.text: Good to see you too, {known_as}.

say: @how_are_things
Yeah? What's up.
Hey. Quick, though. Ice is ticking.

options.text: Why stick and puck?
What brings you to the rink?
What do you make of the rink?
Who else comes out for this?
What would make this place better for you?
Take care.

say: No refs, no score, no yelling. Just the puck and you. It's church.
The sound. Puck off the crossbar. Ping. Best sound there is.
Can't make the beer league schedule. This I can do.

options.text: Makes sense to me.
Tell me a bit about yourself.
Glad you come.
Good to know you, {known_as}.

say: Ice is the ice. Dead board's still dead. That's fine, I like the dead board.
Somebody took my favourite puck. I know it's under the visitors' bench.
@ice

options.text: The ice has been better lately, hasn't it?
Noticed the work on the building?
Fair enough. We're working on it.

say: Ice is quick now. Pucks stay flat. Good work.
Clean sheet. Nobody ruins it at my hour. Perfect.

options.text: Glad it shows.

say: Rooms are better. Showers are hot. Didn't need it, appreciated it.
Fixed the lobby. Fine. I only see it on the way in.

options.text: That's the idea.

say: There's a guy, Hank Lavoie, comes off nights at the mill. Shoots a hundred pucks, never says a word. Hero.
Saw Ronnie Haverstock out here once. Passed off the dead board to himself. I nearly retired.

options.text: Ha. Good to know.

say: More stick and puck. An early slot, every weekday. I'd pay for a card of them.
A punch card for weekday stick and puck. Five bucks a time. I'd never miss.

options.text: I'll see what I can do.
Can't promise anything, but noted.
You're not the first to say it. It's on the list.

say: Back to it. Pucks don't shoot themselves.
Later. Keep the hour, {owner}.
